title: Comparison squares for cocartesian transport
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, equivalence edges and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and coherent composition of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Let $p:E\to B$ be a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories and $f:b_0\to b_1$ an edge of $B$. Put $E_i=E\times_B\{b_i\}$. Choose a coherent cocartesian transport $F:E_0\to E_1$ along $f$, with its coherent lift $\lambda$ from the inclusion of $E_0$ to the inclusion composed with $F$, as supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport]. Let $R:x\to x'$ and $T:y\to y'$ be $p$-cocartesian edges over $f$, with $x,y\in E_0$ and $x',y'\in E_1$. Suppose $u:x\to y$ lies in $E_0$, $v:x'\to y'$ lies in $E_1$, and a coherent square $Tu\simeq vR$ is given over the constant square on $f$ (a map $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to E$ whose composite with $p$ is $f$ on the horizontal coordinate). Then the universal comparisons of cocartesian lifts give equivalences $c_R:F(x)\to x'$ and $c_T:F(y)\to y'$ in $E_1$, with $c_R\lambda_x\simeq R$ and $c_T\lambda_y\simeq T$, and they satisfy
$$v\,c_R\simeq c_T\,F(u)$$
in $E_1$. The comparisons and this compatibility retain their coherent homotopies; $f$ may be degenerate and the color fibers need not be spaces.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 2.4.4.2 and Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category duals (natural mapping-fiber formula and universal comparisons); Proposition 3.1.2.1 dual for coherent transport. This is the comparison-square argument implicit in Higher Algebra, Remark 2.2.4.8, printed p. 212, extracted without operadic hypotheses. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Use the chosen $F$ and $\lambda$ from the statement, rather than choosing a different transport. The vertex components $\lambda_x:x\to F(x)$ and $\lambda_y:y\to F(y)$ are cocartesian. Restricting the simplicial map $E_0\times\Delta^1\to E$ representing $\lambda$ to $u\times\Delta^1$ gives a coherent square over the constant square on $f$, hence $\lambda_yu\simeq F(u)\lambda_x$. The edge $F(u)$ lies in $E_1$. To apply the mapping-space formulation of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] later, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies the horn-cocartesian edges of the hypotheses with the mapping-space-cocartesian edges used in that node. Thus its hypotheses hold for this same $p$ and these same lifts.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.2.1, opposite-category dual, specialized to K=Delta^0 and its coherent transformation component.

proof.text: For the fixed source $x$ and base edge $f$, form the lift category $L(x,f)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Both $\lambda_x:x\to F(x)$ and $R:x\to x'$ are cocartesian lifts of $f$, so both are initial objects of $L(x,f)$. The universal comparison between these initial lifts is an equivalence over $1_{b_1}$; after forgetting the triangle it is an equivalence $c_R:F(x)\to x'$ and gives $c_R\,\lambda_x\simeq R$. Applying the same argument at $y$ to $\lambda_y$ and $T$ gives an equivalence $c_T:F(y)\to y'$ with $c_T\,\lambda_y\simeq T$.

source.place: Remark 2.4.1.9, opposite-category dual: cocartesian lifts are initial in the fixed-source lift category.

proof.text: Put $E_f=E\times_{B,f}\Delta^1$, the degreewise pullback along $f:\Delta^1\to B$, with projection $p_f:E_f\to\Delta^1$; a simplex of $E_f$ is a simplex $\sigma$ of $E$ with a map $\tau:\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$ such that $p\sigma=f\tau$. Since $\Delta^1$ is the nerve of $[1]$, every horn of $\Delta^1$ extends uniquely, so the inner-horn lifting of $p$ gives that $E_f$ is a quasicategory and $p_f$ an inner fibration; the same argument with $\Lambda^n_0$ shows that an edge of $E_f$ whose image in $E$ is $p$-cocartesian is $p_f$-cocartesian. The fibers of $p_f$ over $0$ and $1$ are $E_0$ and $E_1$ (also when $f$ is degenerate, where $\tau$ records the coordinate). Taking $\tau$ to be the horizontal coordinate, the supplied square, the square of Step 1 and the comparison $2$-simplices of Step 2 (which lie over $f$ composed with the degeneracy $\Delta^2\to\Delta^1$ sending $0\mapsto0$, $1,2\mapsto1$) are maps into $E_f$; $\lambda_x,\lambda_y,R,T$ are $p_f$-cocartesian. In $\Delta^1$ the right-pinched mapping spaces from $0$ to $1$ and from $1$ to $1$ have exactly one simplex in each degree, so both are $\Delta^0$. A simplex of $\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(F(x),y')$ has all its vertices over $1$, so its $\tau$ is constant at $1$; hence $\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(F(x),y')=\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(F(x),y')$, and likewise for any two objects of $E_1$.

source.place: Base change of inner fibrations and of (co)cartesian edges along $\Delta^1\to B$ (HTT Remark 2.4.1.4 dual); written out from the definitions.

proof.text:
Choose, in the quasicategory $E_1$, $2$-simplices with edges $(c_R,v,a)$ and $(F(u),c_T,d)$, so $a:F(x)\to y'$ and $d:F(x)\to y'$ are composites $v\,c_R$ and $c_T\,F(u)$ in $E_1$. Work in the homotopy category $hE_f$ of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], in which a $2$-simplex with edges $u,v,w$ gives $[v][u]=[w]$ and composition is associative. The square of Step 1 consists of two $2$-simplices with common diagonal, giving $[\lambda_y][u]=[F(u)][\lambda_x]$; the supplied square gives $[T][u]=[v][R]$; the triangles of Step 2 give $[c_R][\lambda_x]=[R]$ and $[c_T][\lambda_y]=[T]$. Hence in $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(x,y')$
$$[a][\lambda_x]=[v]([c_R][\lambda_x])=[v][R]=[T][u]=[c_T]([\lambda_y][u])=[c_T]([F(u)][\lambda_x])=[d][\lambda_x].$$
The simplices from $E_1$ are simplices of $E_f$, so $[a]=[v][c_R]$ and $[d]=[c_T][F(u)]$ hold in $hE_f$ as well as in $hE_1$.

source.place: Composition in the homotopy category of a quasicategory (Kerodon 4.6.8 / Tag 01PF); applied to the supplied square, the naturality square and the comparison triangles in $E_f$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to the inner fibration $p_f:E_f\to\Delta^1$ of quasicategories, the $p_f$-cocartesian edge $\lambda_x:x\to F(x)$ and $z=y'$. Both base mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(1,1)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(0,1)$ are $\Delta^0$ (Step 3), so the path-space homotopy fiber product of the square is $\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(x,y')\times_{\Delta^0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\Delta^0)\times_{\Delta^0}\Delta^0=\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(x,y')$, and the criterion says that precomposition with $\lambda_x$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(F(x),y')=\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(F(x),y')\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(x,y'),$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. On components it is $[g]\mapsto[g][\lambda_x]$ by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and it is bijective. By Step 4, $[a][\lambda_x]=[d][\lambda_x]$, so $[a]=[d]$ in $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(F(x),y')$: there is a path from $a$ to $d$ in this Kan complex, that is $v\,c_R\simeq c_T\,F(u)$ in $E_1$. No base-path data has to be tracked, because the base mapping spaces of $p_f$ are points.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, opposite-category dual (mapping-space criterion for cocartesian edges), applied to $E_f\to\Delta^1$.

proof.text: The comparisons $c_R,c_T$ come with their triangles and higher simplices as morphisms of $L(x,f)$ and $L(y,f)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]; since their sources are initial, the spaces of such comparisons are contractible, so they are determined up to contractible choice. The compatibility is a path in the Kan complex $\operatorname{Map}_{E_1}(F(x),y')$; since precomposition with $\lambda_x$ is a weak homotopy equivalence (Step 5), paths from $a$ to $d$ correspond up to homotopy to paths from $a\lambda_x$ to $d\lambda_x$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}(x,y')$, among them the one assembled in $E_f$ from the supplied square, the naturality square and the triangles by the composition homotopies of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Nothing requires $f$ to be nondegenerate (Step 3 covers a degenerate $f$), and only mapping spaces are spaces: $E_0,E_1$ need not be.

source.place: Composition and coherence of morphisms, with the initial-lift statement of HTT Proposition 2.4.1.7 / Remark 2.4.1.9 dual.
